utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could we now see on our screens ID 060 D 000316. This is the order of the command of the 1st Military District. It should be in this set that I distributed today. And in number 6. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the defence counsel please repeat the identification number of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. 1D 06, ERN number is 0D 000376. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, have you had occasion to see this order during your stay in Vukovar? First of all, did you ever see this order?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't remember whether I held this in my hands, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In that case, we'll take it item by item and then we'll see whether you can remember it.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: If I can say something? Most often we would receive our orders from the first superior command. However, on very rare occasions, if something was extremely urgent or important, we would receive those orders directly from the higher superior command. And then based on that, we had to draft our own order specifying the tasks of lower subordinate units within the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Danilovic. Now, please be so kind and follow what I read. Item 1. Commands of the 12th Corps, and the first. Proletarian Guards. 3rd Motorised Division. And all commands of units which have their areas of responsibility shall establish town commands in all liberated settlements, officers at the level of battalion commander and above shall be appointed town commanders. Do you know of this order, as to how town commands or local commands were established?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. We have already seen two or three orders previously appointing town commanders for Ovcara, Jakubovac, Grabovo, Sotin and perhaps some other towns where it was necessary to appoint town commanders or local commanders in order to ensure that all requirements necessary for the life and work of units in that area were met.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at item 3. Item 2 specifies the tasks of commands and please look at item 3 and tell me whether item 3 pertains to town commands where there are no civilian organs of authority.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you please read it -- read how town commands are organised in such settlements.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: This item 3 of the order of the 1st Military District, specifies the town commands in settlements where there are no civilian organs of authority shall organise service in town, pursuant to provisions of the rules on service of armed forces pertaining to a garrison, barracks or encampment, in accordance with prevailing conditions in that specific town. In towns where there are no civilian authorities, town commands have the sole responsibility for securing such a town from sabotage operations, as well as ensuring order and safety of citizens. In towns where there are civilian organs of authority, when it comes to issues of order and security, they shall closely cooperate with organs of authority, especially police. This is the content of this item 3 of this order of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We will now go back to item 2, which is the task of the town command. Would you please tell us what were the basic tasks of the town commands.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The basic tasks of the town commands were to establish full military authority in liberated towns; to conduct a census of all military conscripts in their areas of responsibility, to list them all down; until civilian authorities are established, to take measures to ensure order, peace and safety of citizens, ensure basic supplies and other utility services. They are also to work on establishing civilian authorities in municipalities pursuant to the order of Municipal Assembly of Ovcara, that's what it says here. Eastern Slavonia and Western Srem. The following municipalities: Vukovar, Dalj, Vinkovci, with the seat in Mirkovci, and Osijek with a seat in Tenj, as well as in settlements, local communes, and in addition to that, they shall cooperate with TO staffs, police stations and police organs in towns where they exist. This is the task that was give to the town commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Danilovic. Now let us please look at item 7 of this order. Do you see here that they shall report in daily reports about the establishment of town commands?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, in item 7 of this order; that in daily reports they shall report on the establishment of town commands, establishment of organs of authorities, as regulated by the documents, 4614/32 dated 19th of November, 1991, as well as to inform on any problems and dilemmas in relation to these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at item 8. Would you please read it out and tell us what it is about.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Item 8 makes it mandatory for subordinate units as follows: When moving units assigned to town commands, resolve all issues in relation to town commands, which is to say that a new town commander needs to be appointed if the existing unit is leaving that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Danilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suggest -- I, rather, tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 778, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is time for our second break. Our second break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic. And this evening it will be necessary for us to rise at 6.45. We will now resume at ten minutes to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Danilovic, we were talking about the units that were resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade, between the 15th and the 20th of November, 1991. We looked at Exhibit 481 and we realized that the tactical group of the 195th Brigade was resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade with its 450 members. Can we now please look at Exhibit 412. This is another order of the resubordination of a different unit. The ERN is 03502643. That's the B/C/S reference. The English is 03502643. You don't have that in your folder, sir, please look at the monitor. It reads: Regulating the issue of resubordination, order strictly confidential, 405-1, the 15th of November, 1991. Can you please have a look and tell us the interpreter: The interpreters couldn't hear the last part of Mr. Vasic's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This order resubordinate the Stara Pazova detachment and all issues in connection with the resubordination are to be sorted by the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, this is an order of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you remember this unit being subordinated to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade as of the 15th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can we please have a look at a 65 ter document. ID 05, it's the fourth document in the sequence, 0D 000470, this is the same set of documents that we distributed. This is document number 4 in the set. 1D 05 is the number it bears. Thank you. We should have it on our monitors now. Mr. Danilovic, this is an order by the command of the 80th Brigade 40-4, the date is 23rd of November 1991. What exactly is this order about?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a request submitted to the superior command, that is in this case the command of the military district in order to clear the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I think you've got the wrong document. Can you please look at the monitor.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies, really I was looking at the number 4 tab. So this is in reference to the resubordination of units. It's an order to the command of the Stara Pazova TO detachment, in order to successfully implement the decision and order of the exhibits of OG South, strictly confidential 405-1 dated the 15th of November, 1991, and in order to unify command for the following operations resubordinate the following units. Stara Pazova detachment from the 80th Motorised Brigade, shall be resubordinated to the first guards Mechanised division. All issues regarding its resubordination will be regulated by the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, item 2 of this order reads, the Stara Pazova TO detachment shall be carrying out missions in the following operations in keeping with the decision of the commander of the first guards Mechanised division, with a command post in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. This means that the Stara Pazova TO detachment was resubordinated to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Between the 15th of November, as we saw in Exhibit 412, and the 23rd of November and by this order it was resubordinated to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Judge. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I move that this exhibit be admitted into evidence

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 779 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I would like to now move on to a different unit. Can we have Exhibit 420, please. This is 03271247, as the ERN. Thank you very much. Can we zoom in, please. Sir, can you look at the monitor, please and tell me, what sort of an order is this?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I apologies. This is an order by OG South, strictly confidential 446-1, dated the 20th of November, 1991 at 8 o'clock. This is also in reference to regulating issues regarding the resubordination of units. This order is in reference to the armoured battalion of the 544th Motorised Brigade. All issues regarding its resubordination shall be regulated by the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Item 2 reads, until a new assignment is received, the armoured battalion of the 544 Motorised Brigade will be carrying out assignments in keeping with the decision dated 16th of November, 1991. Signed by Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does this order not say that the armoured battalion of the 544 Motorised Brigade is hereby resubordinated to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade on the morning of the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite obviously. There is no doubt about that. Crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the sector in which these units were units that were here, the resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade, the armoured battalion of the 544 Motorised Brigade, the unit that we just spoken about, the Stara Pazova TO detachment, another unit we have mentioned, and the tactical group of the 195 Motorised Brigade. In which area do these units end up after they have been resubordinated to the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: If memory serves, I think these units were in the broader area of Ovcara, roughly speaking. I'm afraid I can't be more specific in the sense of providing a description of how these units were deployed exactly. I do know for a fact that they were in that general area Ovcara, Jakubovac, Grabovo, in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could we see that in the area of responsibility taken over by the 80th Motorised Brigade from the 20th March, Partisan Brigade after the 20th Partisan Brigade had pulled out?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, very much so, this is the very area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will now move on to something completely different. It's about -- again it's about the operations log. If we could please have Exhibit 371, the entry in relation to the 20th of November, at 0900 hours. There's the B/C/S version. In English this is page, page 10. The witness is looking at the B/C/S. Therefore we can have the English page displayed on our monitors, please. Thank you. The 20th of November. We want the 8 o'clock entry. This is the lower half of the page. If we could please zoom in on that. Mr. Danilovic, it says: A group of the brigades officers comprising the Chief of Staff and operative officer, a moral guidance assistant and two clerks as well as the moral guidance assistant were off to the village of Nijemci to take in the -- to calm the situation in the unit which had been involved in the liberation of the villages of Podgradac and Nijemci? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely which it says and that is what happened. I know because I took the group there, as group of officers, command officers brigade command officers pursuant to the order of Lieutenant Vojnovic. If necessary I can elaborate. I can provide further details about the -- about touring the 2nd Motorised Battalion. Its commander was Captain First Class Premovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll not be needing any details about that tour. You went there in order to inspect the situation, right?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We want to know why. It says 8 o'clock in the morning. Was it in the morning that you left to go on that mission?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the morning, yes. It says here 8 o'clock. I'm not sure if it was eight specifically or perhaps half past agent T is sort of difficult for me to pin down that down. But I know it was in the morning hours, early in the morning, you might say. To allow me sufficient time to tour all the battalion units, were this team set up by the brigade commander and in order for me to submit a specific report to him on the situation found in that unit. So that we might be able to take certain steps over the ensuing period of time to calm the situation and raise the combat morale which had been impaired to a significant degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In addition to this group that on the 20th of November, 1991 you led, on this mission, to the village of Nijemci, did anyone else from your unit go there? Did you come across anyone else anyone else from your unit go there? Did you come across anyone else in Nijemci when you were there?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember whether anyone else went there aside from this group of officers that I led. I really can't be expected to remember any detail. It has been a long time, and I would not like to speculate. If there's anything to show what the situation was, if this was recorded any where, maybe we might use that to jog my memory. This way I'm really unable to remember whether anyone else from the 80th Motorised Brigade went there to tour the units, or on a different mission. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We've heard evidence before this Trial Chamber that Captain Jankovic, the commander of the military police company went to Negoslavci that morning, would that jog your memory, sir? Or is it the case that you still can't remember seeing him there?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't confirm that. I can't stretch my memory far enough to remember that. I really don't remember him being there. I remember this group of officers, the chief of engineers, two or three other officers, the moral guidance assistant commander from the brigade command and two clerks from the moral guidance department. That's as much as I can remember, but I would not like to perjure myself or anything, so I simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Just one thing, do you remember Rizmadovic [phoen] being in your group, was he with you?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I remember. I don't remember him being part of our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If you look at the operations log, Exhibit 371, the entry in relation to the 21st of November, 1600 hours. This is page 11 of the English. A group of officers came back from Nijemci that had left the previous day, pursuant to an order of the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Is this entry in reference to your group, and do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do remember by all means.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't hear Mr. Vasic at all. May he please be asked to move closer to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I submitted a detailed oral report to the commander. I really can't remember whether there was a written report too. But I was informed in detail about the situation, about how the battalions units were deployed and the problems that arose during the joint attack with the first Mechanised Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters. I will try to stay closer to the microphone so they can hear me properly. Unfortunately, for that reason, they missed the last portion of my question which was in reference to the report, whether Mr. Danilovic submitted a report to the commander of the 80th Brigade once he was back in Negoslavci, back at the command post in Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've answered that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you please check the entry in relation to 1700 hours, the date still being the 21st of November 1991. This is Page 12. 1700 hours. It reads: Officers arrived with regular reports. I can't read the next word. "Problems"?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Problems and everybody was handed out assignments for recognition. Or for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this briefing on the 21st of November at 1700 hours? Do you remember if anything was said at this briefing about what had occurred in the hanger at Ovcara on the 20th of November, the night between the 20th and the 21st?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not a single word. No reference whatsoever to that unfortunate event. Not as far as I remember. Nothing at all was said about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: While you were away from the brigade command, did you learn anything about what was going on at the Ovcara farm? And I mean the time you spent in the village of Nemci when I say "while you were away".

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The distance is 15 to 20 kilometres, just to err on the side of caution, and there was no way I could know what was going on, nor was I in touch with the brigade commander. Such communication is set up when a brigade is on the move, whenever necessary. Once I was back at the brigade command all I can remember is that there wasn't a single meeting about that, about those problems. Not a single meeting about what had occurred in the village of Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the commander of the 80th Brigade or the chief of security, did they talk to you about what had occurred at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: No. They certainly didn't. I'm certain about that. They might be in a position to confirm that for you, but as far as I remember, we did not discuss that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the area of responsibility of your own brigade, can you tell us if checks were conducted by any of the superior commands within that area as the fighting was still going on and then after the liberation of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: One thing I can say with certainty is that during the attacks, no checks were conducted. There may have been the odd inspection, but after the fall of Vukovar on the 18th of November, inspections became more frequent from our superior commands, inspection teams would come. After that the civilian authorities from Kragujevac and all of those other municipalities would come over to visit conscripts with certain kinds of supplies such as cigarettes, mineral water that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: You say that was after the 18th. Were those inspection teams from OG South? Or from the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the specifics, but I think there were inspections by OG South as well as those conducted by the 1st Military District, as well as our own command, the 24th Kragujevac corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can we please look at Exhibit 371 now, that is in relation to the 22nd of November, 1991, 1700 hours. The English page is -- it's page number 13. What this is about is the commanders of the subordinate units appear to have submitted a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you know if only a regular combat report was submitted on that day, or was there actually a briefing that was held at the command?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, we didn't hear the location that Mr. Vasic mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really can't remember with sure and certain knowledge whether after the regular combat's report had been submitted there was a briefing that was held with subordinate officers from the battalions and divisions in attendance. I really can't say with certainty and I can't be very specific about this. Most frequently briefings were held in the afternoon. Normally at the end of day, about 1800 hours, usually. This was well into November. It got dark sooner and operations would cease. It was at this time of day that commanders would be back to report on what had been done, and then they would be dispatched back to their units with new assignments given then by the brigade commander. However, it was not the established practice for these briefings to take place on a daily basis; that being the reason I can't remember whether there was actually a briefing held on that day, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at one point in time the command of the 80th Brigade took over the area of responsibility of OG South? If so, when?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: All I remember -- well, I'm afraid I can't be very specific, whether it was the 22nd, possibly the 23rd but I think it was one of those days, thereabouts, but I can't say with certainty. I think it was after the 20th of November, that's what I think, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Exhibit 425, please. ERN is 03027149. Can we please have the B/C/S. Thank you. The last portion. This is the OG South command, daily combat report, 22nd of November, 1991. Can we please zoom in on the last two or three paragraphs. It reads: "In the course of the day all measures were taken for the 80th Motorised Brigade to take over the organisational and command function in the area of responsibility of OG South."

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The command of the 80th Motorised Brigade received all the instructions and documents in order to organise control and command in the area of responsibility covered by OG South. My question to you sir, is: Do you know how they clear a memory of when you received this?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received this order and it does jog my memory, but I wasn't sure whether it was the 21st or 22nd or 23rd. I just wasn't prepared to commit. But I know that it was roughly speaking around this time that this handover took place, in terms of the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about the last act in this handover? Isn't it the handover of control and command documents, according to procedure?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most certainly. That is the last act in the handover. The documents are handed off, and then the unit taking over the area of responsibility picks up where the unit on its way out had left off in terms of assignments and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade, Lieutenant Colonel Vojnovic, on the 22nd of November, 1991 issued an order on the transfer of the headquarters to the Vukovar barracks?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that because he told me to set up a group that would see to it that appropriate accommodation was provided. So we went there and this was a barracks where one of the JNA units had been billeted up to 1991, before the well known developments that occurred in Croatia. The barracks itself had been damaged to quite a considerable extent. And this is clear if you look at that document where we request assistance from the command of the 1st Military District to do something about mending the barracks so that it could be used again. Or rather so that the brigade command could be set up in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Speaking of the barracks and your own assignment, the assignment you received from Commander Vojnovic, can we please look at 1D 04, the ERN is 0D 000548, it's a 65 ter document. This is one of the set of documents that we distributed today. It's the number 3. 1D 04. You have it right there in this set, sir. Would you please be so kind as to comment on this order. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: I referred to this order in my own assignment already, the request for clearing the Vukovar barracks. This was submitted to the command of the 1st Military District and the command of the 24th corps, to the attention of -- it says with the objective of clearing the barracks in Vukovar into which the -- or rather it might be a better idea to say, into which the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, from Kragujevac was to be transferred after the final operations regarding the liberation of Vukovar. Please create the prerequisite conditions in order to ensure that there were at least the minimum requirements in place for normal life and work answer winter conditions in these barracks. Then it lists the priorities. It talks about the roof, because most of the roofs were leaking rain because of artillery damage. Item number 2, put up glass panes on all doors and windows on the headquarters' building and the residential facilities. Number 3, repair the water lines and sewer lines in the barracks. This is because there was no water at all, no running water. Item 4, ensure there is central heating and ensure that it is up and running. Number 5, make sure there is enough drinking water in the barracks. And mend the kitchen and the dining room for the units. Number 6, make sure there is electricity in the barracks, because there was no electricity at the time. Number 7, mend the signal centre and make sure it is up and running, and they mean the stationary equipment there. So these were the requests of Commander Vojnovic. Four different things to be mended in these barracks and for assistance to be provided by the superior command which was the command of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The date for this order is the 23rd of November, 1991; isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes indeed that is what it says. Indeed, that is the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind this list of requests, of roofs that were damaged, windows smashed, no running water, no electricity, no sewer lines, was those barracks fit to hold so many people now that you arrived, given the conditions that prevailed at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at our request, it is quite obvious that the conditions that prevailed in the barracks at the time were, what shall I call them, the barracks was not safe for holding so many people and that no proper working conditions were in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 780, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We were saying a little while ago that the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade took over responsibility in an area covered by OG South. Did your command at a moment in time become town commander, of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe there is a -- there is a relevant order. As we were the highest ranking command in the city of Vukovar it was logical for the command -- commander, commanders of the brigade to become the command of that town also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, were the tasks of your command in accordance with those from the order of the 1st Military District that referred to the establishment of military authority in the whole area and maintaining law and order and security for the population?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. The command of the brigade invested huge efforts into the organisation and the establishment of civilian authority. I don't remember whether it was the General Staff or the command of the 1st Military District, but I know, for certain, that two or three officers arrived to assist us in the establishment of civilian authority in the city of Vukovar. And we wanted to transfer some responsibilities to civilian authorities. I think that Lieutenant Colonel Milo Stojakovic was there, and if I remember well there were two more officers assisting in the establishment of civilian authority after the cessation of combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Could we now take a look at Exhibit 371 entry for 8 o'clock, 24 of November. The witness has the B/C/S version. I would like the English version on the screen. It is on page 14. That's the operations log of the 80th Motorised Brigade. So the entry is dated 24th of November, 800 hours, on page 14. This says the commander and the Chief of Staff are leaving for an inspection of units at Vukovar -- and an inspection of Vukovar barracks for the purpose of the accommodation of staff units, activities on the organisation of military authority in Vukovar. Can you tell us, what kind of inspection of the staff of the TO Vukovar and police this was. Can you elaborate what those duties were that the commander had.

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: The staff of the Territorial Defence was not subordinate to the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade, but that command cooperated very closely with that staff, assisting them to achieve -- to accomplish their tasks. That staff established that police station, if I remember well, the last name of that police officer was Travnica, and he carried out his tasks very seriously, and I remember meeting him several times for coordination purposes, and we also secured some buildings in the city. We organised patrols, or, rather, check-points in town, since there were still individual instances of members of the ZNG and MUP of the Republic of Croatia pulling out of there, out from the town of Vukovar and its suburbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The cooperation with the staff of TO Vukovar, whose responsibility was it from your command?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, often times that responsibility was assumed by the brigade commander. I think that I, too, went to that staff sometimes, but I really couldn't give you the details since it's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: There are entries in the operations log about that. We needn't go into all of those entries. Now, the Court can check that. So much about the Staff of TO Vukovar. We can continue. Tell me, do you know that the commander of the staff of TO Vukovar was wounded at a certain point in time, and do you know that a report was submitted to the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: RADE DANILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that Miomir Vujevic was wounded by his escort from a Skorpion automatic pistol. 7.65 millimetres calibre. The superior command was informed of it, and he was transferred, as far as I remember, to VMA in Belgrade. I think it was a wound in the stomach, but I really never received any feedback about that incident. So I don't know whether it was an accident or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the 6th document, 1D 07. So 1D 000511, or perhaps we should leave this document for tomorrow, as it is already 6.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. We will need to do it tomorrow and resume tomorrow at 9 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Presiding Judge, I want to have a request. I would like to, to greet Mr. Sljivancanin and Mr. Radic, if you will allow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid that is not permitted while you are giving your evidence. That will have to wait until you conclude your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of September, 2006 at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [The accused, Radic and Sljivancanin enter court]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.45 p.m.,
